title: Atlas and Orchard
premise: In 1918, in a river town whose only bridge out of the valley closes each winter, Noor Vasquez inherits his murdered master's unfinished atlas and the dangerous truth hidden in its margins: the maps prove the army has been falsifying border lines to seize farmland. When the bridge shuts for the season, Noor is trapped with the atlas, his sister Amaya's family, and Captain Reyes — the officer who may have ordered the master's death but now needs Noor's maps to negotiate an armistice. As spring thaws approach, Noor must decide who among his family takes the last berth on the final ferry before the armistice is signed or collapses, while choosing whether to trade the atlas's proof for their safety or release it to the valley that made him. He gives up the berth himself, publishes the true borders, and stays — finding belonging not in escape but in the place he finally maps as home.
about_author: Juniper Galloway is the pen name of a former cartographic archivist who spent a decade restoring war-damaged maps from border regions. She writes historical fiction about the people who draw lines on paper and the people who live inside them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Noor Vasquez, POV. In the mapmaker's locked workshop, Noor begins finishing the atlas his master Elias died for, discovering sealed folios he was never meant to open. The emotional beat is grief braided with curiosity — love for a dead mentor pulling him toward a secret that will cost him everything.

chapters.title: Margins in Red Ink
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Hidden beneath the official border lines, Noor finds Elias's corrections proving the army redrew the valley's boundaries to dispossess farming families. Fear arrives: this knowledge killed Elias. The beat is dawning dread as apprenticeship becomes inheritance of danger.

chapters.title: Orders Come Down
chapters.summary: Amaya, POV. Noor's sister Amaya receives evacuation papers granting her family berths on the last pre-armistice ferry out of the valley. She hides them from Noor, torn between loyalty and escape. The beat is maternal ferocity sharpened by guilt over what she's concealing.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Winter storms close the bridge — the only road out — stranding the town with soldiers garrisoned at its foot. Among the officers is Captain Reyes, whom Noor recognizes from the night Elias died. The beat is claustrophobia; the world shrinks to one frozen crossing.

chapters.title: A Guest in Uniform
chapters.summary: Reyes, POV. Reyes requisitions the workshop, claiming he needs accurate maps for armistice negotiations — and revealing he knows the atlas contains the true borders. His interiority shows a man obeying orders he despises. The beat is uneasy mutual recognition between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Amaya, POV. Amaya packs the household, measuring every possession by whether it can be carried, while pressing Noor to burn the atlas and take a berth. Their first quarrel splits duty to family against duty to truth. The beat is love expressed as argument.

chapters.title: The Ferry Manifest
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Noor learns there are three berths left, not four — someone must stay behind. He studies the manifest like a chart, plotting lives instead of coastlines. The beat is quiet horror as cartography becomes triage.

chapters.title: Elias's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. A letter sewn into the atlas's spine reveals Elias knew he would die and chose Noor as heir deliberately, writing 'a map is a promise; keep mine.' The beat is devastating tenderness that converts fear into resolve.

chapters.title: Negotiation at the Bridgehead
chapters.summary: Reyes, POV. Reyes offers Noor protection and ferry passage for his whole family in exchange for surrendering the original corrected maps — which he will then destroy to preserve the army's fiction. The beat is temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: The Valley Remembers
chapters.summary: Amaya, POV. Amaya walks the farmland slated for seizure, hearing neighbors' stories of deeds and graves the new maps erase. She begins to understand what Noor is carrying. The beat is reluctant conversion from escape to witness.

chapters.title: Frozen Crossing
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Noor attempts a night reconnaissance of the frozen river as an alternative route out, nearly dies when the ice cracks, and is saved by a soldier sympathetic to the farmers. The beat is humility — the land itself refuses to be mapped by force.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Reyes, POV. Reyes confronts his superior, General Aldana, and is threatened with Elias's fate. Alone, he copies fragments of the true borders, no longer sure which side of the line he stands on. The beat is a conscience cracking under pressure.

chapters.title: The Berth Decision
chapters.summary: Amaya, POV. With the thaw weeks away, Amaya forces the question: who takes the last berth? She names herself, then her children, then begs Noor to choose so she doesn't have to. The beat is the novel's moral fulcrum — love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: Counterfeit Coastlines
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Noor begins forging a false atlas to hand Reyes while hiding the real one, using every trick Elias taught him. The work steadies him; deception becomes devotion. The beat is craft as resistance, tension humming under precision.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Archive
chapters.summary: Reyes, POV. Reyes detects the forgery within hours — he trained under Elias too — but says nothing, instead warning Noor that Aldana plans to search the workshop after the armistice signing. The beat is alliance forming across enemy lines.

chapters.title: The Night of Copies
chapters.summary: Noor and Amaya, alternating. Siblings work together printing duplicates of the true maps to seed through the valley before any search, mending their quarrel in ink and lamplight. The beat is reconciliation — family redefined as shared purpose.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. The ice breaks; the bridge reopens; Aldana's men move on the workshop. Noor sends the atlas downstream hidden in a survey crate while soldiers ransack shelves behind him. The beat is breathless sacrifice — the master's promise escaping by water.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Amaya, POV. At the dock, Amaya puts her children aboard, then shoves her own berth papers into Noor's hands. He refuses and gives them to the orphaned apprentice Tomas instead. The beat is the blurb's choice answered: no one trades family; they widen it.

chapters.title: Armistice, Signed or Not
chapters.summary: Reyes, POV. At the bridgehead signing, Reyes produces the copied true borders publicly, forcing Aldana's line to collapse; the armistice holds only because the lie cannot. The beat is justice outside the law, paid for with Reyes's career.

chapters.title: Reading the River
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. The atlas surfaces downstream in a newspaper office; the valley's farms are restored to the maps. Noor, passed over for arrest because the truth is now public, walks the land Elias died defending. The beat is vindication without triumph.

chapters.title: Home Coordinates
chapters.summary: Amaya, POV. Amaya returns from the ferry landing having chosen to stay; the family reunites in the repaired workshop, measuring nothing by what can be carried anymore. The beat is belonging earned — home as a place you refuse to abandon.

chapters.title: Atlas and Orchard
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Years later, Noor completes the atlas, adding one final plate: the orchard behind the workshop, drawn in Elias's hand and his own. He teaches Tomas the trade, promising maps that tell the truth. The beat is resolution — legacy, love, and lines drawn honestly.
